steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Retry with exponential backoff** in *Retries with backoff*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: int Delay(int n, int baseMs, int capMs) => (int)Math.Min(capMs, baseMs * Math.Pow(2, n - 1));

steps.title: Rebuild Retry with exponential backoff cold
prompt: The tests declare `IClock` / `FakeClock` (as in the previous lesson; `Sleep` records the delay and moves time on).
Write `(int Status, int Attempts) Execute(Func<int> call, int maxAttempts, int baseDelayMs, int capDelayMs, IClock clock)`:
- call `call()`; it returns a status code (`0` = no response);
- if the status is `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` or `0` and attempts remain, `clock.Sleep(delay)` and try again, with `delay = min(cap, base × 2^(n−1))` for the n-th retry;
- never sleep after the last attempt; any other status returns immediately;
- return the last status and how many attempts were made.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
(int Status, int Attempts) Execute(Func<int> call, int maxAttempts, int baseDelayMs, int capDelayMs, IClock clock)
